title: Why Linux is making a comeback on desktop in 2026

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Linux is reclaiming the desktop because it's the only OS that doesn't lock users out of their own systems. (3 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: You're ignoring the reality that Linux now supports full GPU acceleration via Vulkan and Wayland, making it competitive with Windows. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: With Flatpak and Snap, Linux now has universal app packaging—something Windows still struggles with across different versions. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Major companies like Red Hat and Canonical are investing billions in desktop Linux, proving it's no longer a niche choice. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Linux is the future of the desktop—open, secure, and built for developers and power users. (4 sec)
